label: Origin-tolerance rival with varied individual restored, against actual-world Euclidean access
summary: Closes the interpretation gap of the structural surrogate ToleranceOriginRival.Control.Certificate. Added an origin interface (OriginToleranceIdentity): origins per world and individual, a closeness relation near; commitments NearIsTolerance (reflexive, symmetric), OriginDeterminesAccess (access iff every shared individual has near origins), OriginPlenitude (every near variation realised in an accessible world) and VariedOriginAt (one actual concrete individual with non-near origins at two successors). Bridge originToleranceNonEuclidean (zero-axiom): NearIsTolerance, OriginDeterminesAccess and VariedOriginAt entail the surrogate frame condition ToleranceNonEuclideanAt. Outcome on the surrogate: restoring the varied individual at all three offsets (Control.restored) satisfies the four commitments but the individual exists at every successor of actual, so NecessaryConcreteAt holds there: the surrogate countermodel is destroyed under the restored commitment. Outcome on Arrival A: a faithful countermodel survives on five worlds with two rigidly identified individuals (Control.faithful): a with offsets -1/0/+1 at aMinus/actual/plus, b with offsets 0/0/-1/+1 at actual/plus/bMinus/bPlus; access fails only aMinus-plus and bMinus-bPlus. All four origin commitments, ActualReflexive, presence-to-existence, inert emptiness and the possible contingent-free past (witness plus, times 0<1: b necessary at plus and present throughout, a contingent at plus and present only at 1) hold; EuclideanAt and NecessaryConcreteAt fail at actual (a absent from bMinus, b absent from aMinus). General reason: the arrival delivers an individual necessary relative to the witness world v; without Euclidean access nothing forces it into a successor of actual that v does not see, and origin tolerance permits such a successor (the far-origin world of another individual) to lack it. Why two individuals (prose argument, not Lean-checked): under OriginDeterminesAccess, if c is necessary at v and u is a successor of actual lacking c, then v does not see u, so some individual y existing at v and u has far origins there; y differs from c since c is absent from u. Correction after semantic challenge: any countermodel to Arrival A needs two individuals, already forced by the arrival's premises (necessary-at-v and contingent-at-v individuals differ); the origin argument adds that the c-lacking successor must be cut off by a second individual's far origin; on a one-individual carrier the arrival's premises are unsatisfiable, so it holds only vacuously. Control.restored covers one assignment; the general three-world case is prose. Strongest objection (challenge), as corrected in the cycle-4 repair: deletion at actual (every actual concrete individual is absent from some world accessible from actual) holds in Control.faithful itself and excludes only an actual necessary concrete individual, not necessity relative to other worlds (b exists at plus and every successor of plus). Worldwise deletion (the same at every world) fails in Control.faithful at plus; with the arrival's presence, inertness and contingent-free-past premises it is inconsistent, because InertEmptiness.earlierNecessary supplies a necessary concrete individual at the temporal witness world (checked composition pending). That is an incompatibility of the strengthened bundle: it does not make the five-world model of the original bundle vacuous and does not defeat the rival under its encoded commitments. Whether origin tolerance warrants worldwise deletion is a separate open warrant question.
blocker: The countermodel uses permitted, not required, absences (b from aMinus, a from bMinus); OPEN whether a cross-world persistence bridge (an individual necessary at a possible world exists at every possibility of actual) is warranted independently of Euclidean access, and whether the if-half of OriginDeterminesAccess is part of the account. Counterpart, vague and kind-relative tolerance readings and the possible-external-cause arrival were not tested.
